title: Normalized Evidence

evidenceReference.x-evidence-key-invariant: evidenceKey is the lowercase SHA-256 of PBGC Case Workbench Canonicalization Profile v1 deterministic {artifactSha256, citationId, sourceLocator, evidenceKind, observedTextOrValue when present}; evidenceKey itself and all operational metadata are excluded. Strings undergo NFC preprocessing; object keys, JSON numbers, nested arrays, null, and absence follow the profile. The reference resolves by evidenceKey to exactly one manifest-local populationEvidenceObservation that has the same evidenceKey and agrees on every deterministic field and canonical byte.
evidenceReference.x-exact-decimal-rule: A value whose lexical decimal precision is material must be represented as a canonical decimal string matching governed-records.schema.json#/$defs/canonicalDecimalString, never as a JSON number.

populationEvidenceObservation.x-evidence-key-invariant: evidenceKey is the single identity shared with PopulationCandidate evidence references and is the lowercase SHA-256 of PBGC Case Workbench Canonicalization Profile v1 deterministic {artifactSha256, citationId, sourceLocator, evidenceKind, observedTextOrValue when present}; the key and operational metadata are excluded. Absence differs from null. Each evidenceKey and citationId is unique in the registry, and artifactSha256 resolves to exactly one manifest artifact.

populationCandidate.x-candidate-key-invariant: candidateKey is the lowercase SHA-256 of PBGC Case Workbench Canonicalization Profile v1 deterministic PopulationCandidate content excluding candidateKey and operational/computed fields. Only values explicitly typed by a schema as PopulationCandidate receive the intrinsic evidence-set rule: validate evidenceKey, sort by evidenceKey then canonical item bytes, and reject duplicate keys/content and indistinguishable elements. Object shape alone never confers the type. artifactSha256 must equal an enclosing normalized-evidence sourceSha256 when applicable. Changed candidate or evidence content changes the applicable evidenceKey and candidateKey.

x-deterministic-array-semantics.deterministicPayload.observations: order-significant; preserve parser-declared source order established by source locator and occurrence; implementations must not reorder
x-deterministic-array-semantics.deterministicPayload.populationCandidate: set-like; validate each lowercase evidenceKey against canonical deterministic evidence-reference content, sort ascending by evidenceKey then canonical item bytes, and reject duplicate evidenceKey, duplicate canonical content, indistinguishable normalized elements, malformed keys, and stale artifact/citation/location references; null evidence items are invalid and absence of the required array is invalid
order-significant; preserve physical source-field order; implementations must not reorder
order-significant; positions correspond to the preserved source sheet/section order
x-deterministic-array-semantics.validationResults: set-like; sort by validationKey then canonical item bytes; reject duplicate validationKey

x-intrinsic-type-array-semantics.PopulationCandidate.evidence: set-like wherever a schema explicitly types the value as PopulationCandidate; sort by evidenceKey ascending then PBGC Case Workbench Canonicalization Profile v1 item bytes; reject duplicate evidenceKey, duplicate canonical content, and indistinguishable elements. Candidate-shaped arbitrary objects are not duck typed and use ordinary recursive rules.

x-canonicalization-profile: PBGC Case Workbench Canonicalization Profile v1
x-numeric-canonicalization: All deterministic JSON numbers use RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme number serialization over finite IEEE-754 binary64 values: equivalent inputs such as 1, 1.0, and 1e0 serialize identically; negative zero serializes as 0; NaN and infinities are invalid; source-language lexical formatting is never hashed. Exact decimals whose lexical precision is material use canonical decimal strings instead.
x-recursive-deterministic-json: Object keys canonicalize recursively. Intrinsic type-level array rules apply in every embedding and cannot be overridden by a generic fallback. Arrays at exact registered paths use those rules. Every otherwise-unregistered array, including arrays nested at any depth inside observedValue, normalizedValue, or evidence objects, is order-significant by default and preserves element order. Exact path rules do not propagate to descendants.
